transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining. I want to use part of today's weekly operating review to address the escalation handoff issues between Client Operations and Implementation. Lina and Omar, you both currently share responsibility for these handoffs, and I understand there's been ongoing disagreement about who communicates with the client versus who owns the internal follow-up. With the major client rollout starting in just four weeks, we need a stable, clear process in place well before then. I'd like to hear from both of you about where the friction is happening, and then I'll make a decision on how we restructure the responsibility and adjust our coordination process going forward. Who wants to start?

transcript.text: Thank you both for the transparency. Lina, I appreciate you surfacing the expired informal agreement — that explains a lot of the ambiguity we've been seeing. Omar, I note your point about capacity and your request for a separate conversation; we'll absolutely make time for that after we resolve the process question today. You're both right that whatever we decide needs to be documented this time. Before I make a decision on restructuring, I want to make sure I have the full picture. Omar, you mentioned your current capacity directly affects what you can reliably commit to for the next four weeks. Can you share what that capacity situation looks like so I can factor it into the responsibility structure? And Lina, beyond the expired agreement, are there any other specific friction points — around handoff timing or support needs — that you think the new arrangement needs to address?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Thanks, Priya. A couple of specific friction points beyond the expired agreement: First, on handoff timing — there's no defined trigger for when an escalation officially moves from Client Operations to Implementation. We've been using judgment calls, which means sometimes the client gets contacted twice and sometimes not at all until well after the issue surfaces. Second, on communication ownership — even during the six-week informal period, it wasn't clear who owned the client update when an escalation spanned multiple days. I'd own the initial communication, but if root-cause work stretched into day two or three, it was unclear whether I stayed the client point of contact or Omar picked it up. Third, on support needs — when Omar's team is at capacity, there's no documented fallback, so I end up either holding the client too long or escalating informally, which creates its own confusion. I think the new arrangement needs to define a clear handoff trigger, single-point client ownership regardless of duration, and a documented fallback for when Implementation capacity is constrained.

What I can commit to within those constraints: I can own the internal root-cause follow-up as before, and I can meet the Tuesday 14:00 slot consistently.
